# tracecontext — spec

## Maturity

**Grade:** 1 · S1 E1 A1 H1 P1 *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** ahead — W3C Trace Context Level 1 + OpenTelemetry `TraceContext` propagator (surveyed 2026-09-30, gaps closed 2026-10-11; lead on the `**Ahead:**` line 2026-10-24)

**Ahead:** correctness — OpenTelemetry Go v1.46.0 `propagation.TraceContext`, the propagator the reference spec is measured against here (the `**Performance:**` reference), breaks three W3C rules on the oracle's own request headers (`tools/go_oracle`, re-taken 2026-10-24 by `tools/interop.zig --check`): it drops the whole trace on unknown trace-flags bits (`…-ff`, `…-09`; W3C: accept and zero them on the way out), reads only the first of two `tracestate` fields (W3C: combine them, RFC 9110 §5.3 — a second vendor's state is lost) and drops the whole `tracestate` list on one duplicated key (the W3C suite's `test_tracestate_duplicated_keys` requires it kept); this module does all three as specified (test "otel oracle: the middleware continues, restarts and carries state as OpenTelemetry Go does", divergences shape02 shape04 sub53f sub54f state_split state27) (measured 2026-10-24)

**Audit:** review 2026-10-24 · mutation 2026-10-24 (73/76, 3 eq) · src c4f6e467cb42376b

**Hardening:** fuzz 2026-10-09 (200,000-run budget per harness clean, TRACECONTEXT_FUZZ) · ct n/a — trace id headers (keyword review, 2026-10-07)

**Performance:** ref 0.26–0.40× OpenTelemetry Go v1.46.0 TraceContext · fastest 0.78× OpenTelemetry Rust 0.33.1 `TraceContextPropagator` (row `propagate`, net of each side's HTTP stack — httparse + `http::Request` on the Rust side; `state` 0.67×, `fresh` 0.54×; `tools/rust_fast_bench`) (measured 2026-10-24)

**Where we are ahead:** a small dependency-free HTTP middleware that needs no tracer or SDK: continue-or-start with a fresh span-id per hop, `tracestate` carried through per RFC 9110 header combining, forward-compatible parse of higher `traceparent` versions, a vendored W3C conformance corpus with a count canary, a fuzz target and a never-panics parse on arbitrary bytes. **Where we are behind:** nothing a user of the OpenTelemetry `TraceContext` propagator would miss since 2026-10-11: `tracestate` is parsed by the member grammar with the 32-member cap, members can be read, added (moved to the front), updated and deleted (`TraceState`), and the middleware writes this service's own entry (`Options.state_entry`). Not here, by design: W3C Baggage (a separate spec and a separate OTel propagator — a sibling module if wanted, Backlog), span/tracer/exporter (propagation only), Level 2 (`random-trace-id`; not a recommendation yet). Different from otel where W3C says otherwise: unknown flag bits accepted and zeroed, duplicated `traceparent` restarts, split `tracestate` fields combined, a duplicated `tracestate` key keeps the left one (otel drops the list; the W3C suite requires it kept).

## Design & invariants
`traceparent` shape: `version-traceid-parentid-flags` — version two lowercase hex (`00`/Level 1 emitted;
a higher version read forward-compatibly as its Level 1 prefix, `ff` rejected), trace-id 16 bytes/32 hex (all-zero invalid), parent-id/span-id 8 bytes/16 hex (all-zero
invalid), flags one byte/2 hex (bit 0 = sampled). Per request: a valid incoming `traceparent` (when
`trust_incoming`) is *continued* — its trace-id and its `sampled` flag are kept (every other flag
bit is zeroed on the way out: "Vendors MUST set all unparsed / unknown trace-flags to 0 on outgoing
requests"; an incoming `…-ff` is accepted, never refused, and goes out `…-01`), but a fresh span-id
is minted for this hop; absent or malformed input starts a new trace. `tracestate` (only with a
continued `traceparent`) is combined across fields and parsed by `TraceState.parse`: the key grammar
`(lcalpha / DIGIT) 0*255(keychar)` with keychar `a-z 0-9 _ - * / @` (the pinned spec revision's text;
Level 1's `tenant@system` split is a subset), values of 1–256 characters in 0x20–0x7E without `,`/`=`
and not ending in a space; OWS around members and empty members ignored; more than 32 members or any
bad member drops the whole list; a key's later duplicates are dropped (the left one is the most
recent). Out goes the re-serialized list, with `Options.state_entry`'s member put in front (replacing
ours, dropping the right-most when 32 are already there), on a new trace too. More than 512
characters out: whole members left out, over-128-character ones first, then from the right. Register first (outermost) so every
response carries the context. `current()` exposes the current hop's context (thread-local, mirroring
`requestid.current()`); when `echo` is set the outgoing header is written back on the response.
`TraceParent.parse`/`.write`/`.sampled`, `childOf`, `newTrace`, `newTraceId`, `newSpanId` are usable
standalone, no HTTP. Generated IDs come from one process-wide atomic sequence offset by a
per-process prefix and scattered by a 64-bit bijection (SplitMix64's finalizer) — unique within the
process across threads; a trace-id carries the prefix itself in its first 8 bytes. No allocation,
no OS entropy call (W3C Level 1 requires trace-ids to be *unique*, not random). Memory/concurrency:
current context is a value in thread-local storage owned by the connection task
(task-per-connection: one request at a time per thread); the outgoing `tracestate` is formatted
into a thread-local buffer valid until the next request on the thread; config is immutable after init
(threadsafe). Clean-room from the W3C Trace Context Level 1 recommendation — see NOTICE.

## Threat model / out of scope
Like `requestid`, the generated ids are **correlation** identifiers, explicitly not unpredictable
security tokens — do not rely on trace-id/span-id being unguessable; mint your own CSPRNG id and set
`traceparent` yourself if that matters. Trusting an incoming `traceparent` is opt-in
(`trust_incoming`) and validated only for wire shape, not provenance — the trust boundary (only
accept it from a trusted upstream proxy) is the caller's network topology. Only Level 1 is
implemented — no Level 2 (not yet published), no vendor-specific `tracestate` interpretation, no
sampling-decision logic beyond forwarding/setting the `sampled` bit, no span export/collector
integration (propagation only, not a tracer). An incoming `tracestate` longer than 512 characters
combined is dropped whole (W3C asks vendors to document their maximum; this is it), so an upstream
that sends more loses the whole list here rather than its tail.

A `traceparent` version higher than `"00"` is parsed forward-compatibly (since 2026-08-02), as
the spec's "Versioning of traceparent" asks: the fixed-position trace-id, parent-id and sampled
bit are trusted when the header is long enough and correctly delimited, and the rest is ignored;
version `ff` is invalid. Pinned by the test "a future traceparent version is parsed as its
Level 1 prefix" and by the W3C suite's `test_traceparent_version_0xcc` vectors in
`src/w3c_vectors.zig`.

## Verification
Offline unit tests through `http.Server.serveStream`: valid incoming traceparent carried into the
child (fresh span-id) with `current()` agreement, absent/malformed inputs start a fresh valid trace,
duplicated-traceparent rejection, multi-instance `tracestate` combining + OWS handling, `echo=false`,
parse/write round-trip, invalid inputs rejected (bad version, length, delimiter, uppercase hex,
all-zero ids), `childOf` plus id uniqueness/non-zero. PLUS a vendored W3C `trace-context`
conformance corpus (`src/w3c_vectors.zig` + `src/w3c_conformance_test.zig`; provenance in
this module's `NOTICE`): 73 hand-transcribed request/verdict vectors from the suite's `test/test.py`,
69 driven both must-accept and must-reject through this module's own middleware, 4 excluded with a
recorded reason apiece (a count canary fails loudly on unreclassified drift). Run: `zig build
test-tracecontext`.

**tracestate grammar and own entry (2026-10-11).** The suite's 8 STRICT_LEVEL 2 vectors (illegal key
characters, `@`-first key, 33 members, 257-character key, `=` in a value, empty value) are asserted
now, and the 4 duplicated-key vectors expect the left member kept (upstream accepts kept-as-is or
one discarded). The OpenTelemetry oracle's divergences fell from 27 to 12: the 14 grammar ones agree
now; left are digit-first keys and `a@=1` (valid by the pinned W3C key grammar, not by otel's) and a
duplicated key (otel drops the list, W3C keeps it). `TraceState` tests: normalization, dedup, `put`
moves left, `delete`, the 32-member cap on input and on `put`, the key/value grammar edges, and
truncation on write (over-128 first — negative control: right-most only fails it). `state_entry`:
our member first, replacing a stale one, the only member of a new trace, a bad value not added.
Seeded model-fuzz: 3000 random lists (0–35 members, OWS, empty members, duplicates, bad keys and
values) against a naive restatement of the grammar, plus write→parse round trip (negative control:
a 33-member cap crashes it). Generated ids: no duplicate trace-id or span-id among 6400 each from 32
threads at once (negative control: a thread-local sequence fails it).

**Audit 2026-10-04 (mutation).** 22 schemata mutants over `TraceParent.parse` (version
`ff`, `00` exact length, future-version delimiter, all three field delimiters, zero ids,
uppercase hex), `write`/`sampled`/`childOf`, the middleware (`trust_incoming`, `sampled`,
`echo`, tracestate only with a parsed parent, duplicate traceparent) and `isValidState` /
`combinedHeader`: 22 killed, 0 equivalent, 0 left alive. Four survivors of the first run
got tests: a non-dash at byte 35 and at byte 52 (W3C Trace Context §3.2.2), a fresh trace
under `Options.sampled = false` is unsampled, and DEL in a tracestate fails `isValidState`
(replaced 2026-10-11 by the member grammar; the DEL test now holds `isValidValue`)
(asserted on the guard itself: `http.Server`'s h1 parser already refuses a header value with
DEL, so the wire cannot reach it).

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle EXTERNAL

- **Class A** — wire/interop format — other implementations must byte-agree with it.
- **Oracle EXTERNAL** — every path's expected values come from an implementation that is not ours.

**What the tests actually contain.** src/w3c_conformance_test.zig drives the middleware through 73 vendored W3C trace-context conformance vectors (src/w3c_vectors.zig) in both directions over the real offline wire harness; src/otel_oracle_test.zig replays OpenTelemetry Go's TraceContext propagator (otel v1.46.0, `tools/go_oracle/` → `otel_vectors.zig`) on 498 request-header sets of ours — traceparent shapes incl. future versions (forward-compatible parsing), every single-character substitution of a valid header, duplicated fields, 43 tracestate shapes with and without a parent, split fields — through the same middleware: continue where otel continues (same trace-id, same sampled bit), restart where it restarts, carry the list members it keeps, never send an unknown flag bit, and refuse (400) a field with a control character. 12 listed divergences (27 until the 2026-10-11 member grammar), each decided by the W3C text or its conformance suite (otel refuses unknown flags, reads only the first of duplicated/split fields, accepts `00-…-01-`, drops a list with a duplicated key or a digit-first key). Self only: trace-id/span-id GENERATION (randomness has no outside answer; non-zero and uniqueness are held by the module's own tests); Level 2 is out of scope

**OpenTelemetry oracle 2026-10-05.** One defect, fixed the same day: unknown trace-flags bits were propagated (`childOf` copied the whole byte, so an incoming `…-ff` went out `…-ff`), where W3C requires them zeroed on outgoing requests.

**How it got there.** The anchoring work landed. DONE e269090: 73 W3C vectors; found MUST-not-parse-tracestate bug; 1 gap logged
